plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if rivals bid high; underbidding risks losing when winning would yield positive profit. With no informative history and values uniform on [0,49], I will bid exactly my value ($13). If I win, expected payment equals the second-highest bid; profit is 13 minus that amount, else zero.

[ With independent private values and a second-price (pay the second-highest bid) format, bidding truthfully is a weakly dominant strategy. By bidding my value ($49), I maximize expected profit: I win whenever my value is the highest and pay the second-highest bid, yielding non-negative surplus. Any bid below 49 risks losing profitable wins; any bid above 49 risks winning when the second price exceeds my value. Ties, if any, are resolved randomly; truthful bidding still maximizes expected payoff. No prior history to exploit in round 1 of 1. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction. With independent private values and risk-neutrality, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value, regardless of others’ strategies. Discretization to $0.1 doesn’t change this here since 44.0 is exactly representable. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit by ensuring you win whenever it’s profitable (when opponents’ max bid is below 44) and pay the second-highest bid. No past history to adjust for in this single round. ]
